title: Motovun Travel Guide: Truffles, Parking & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Motovun, Croatia. Find the best places to stay, driving routes, parking information, and tips for visiting this Istrian hilltop town.
intro:
Motovun is a medieval hilltop town in central Istria, located above the Mirna River valley. It appeals to food enthusiasts, wine drinkers, and visitors seeking a quiet base away from the coastal resorts. The town is widely known for the surrounding truffle forests, local vineyards producing Teran and Malvasia wines, and intact 13th-century defensive walls that offer views across the region.

The town requires physical mobility to navigate, as the historic center is situated on a steep incline and is strictly car-free. Most visitors arrive between late spring and early autumn, with October being particularly popular for the white truffle harvest. Because it is located inland, a vehicle is highly recommended for reaching the town, exploring neighboring agricultural estates, and visiting the coast, which is roughly a 40-minute drive away.

areas.name: Motovun Old Town
areas.parking: None at accommodation; use municipal lots below
areas.summary: The walled medieval center at the top of the hill. Access requires walking up a steep cobblestone path or taking a municipal shuttle from the lower parking areas.

areas.name: Kanal (Foot of Motovun)
areas.bestFor: Road trippers and visitors with mobility concerns
areas.parking: Easy, mostly free private parking at properties
areas.summary: The settlement located at the base of the hill near the Mirna River. It offers straightforward parking, flat terrain, and quick access to regional roads while keeping the old town in view.

areas.name: Livade
areas.summary: A small village situated directly across the valley from Motovun. It serves as the commercial center of the Istrian white truffle industry and features notable local restaurants.

areas.name: Kaldir
areas.parking: Ample private parking on farms and estates
areas.summary: A rural village 5 kilometers southeast of Motovun. It is recognized for its fruit orchards, vineyards, and traditional farm stays (agroturizam).

whenToGo: July and August are the hottest months with daytime temperatures often exceeding 30°C, and they represent the busiest time for day-trippers visiting from coastal resorts. Sea temperatures at the nearby coast peak at 25°C to 27°C. May, June, and September offer milder temperatures around 20°C to 25°C, lower accommodation prices, and fewer crowds. October and November mark the highly anticipated white truffle season, bringing food enthusiasts to the region; most restaurants remain open, though days are considerably shorter and cooler. From December to March, the weather is cold and damp, many hotels and restaurants close for the season, and the town is very quiet.

faq.question: Is Motovun worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, Motovun is worth visiting for its well-preserved medieval architecture, panoramic views of the Mirna Valley, and distinct local food culture. It serves as an excellent inland contrast to Istria's busier coastal resorts.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Motovun?
faq.answer: One full day is enough to walk the city walls, explore the historic center, and eat at a local restaurant. However, many visitors stay three to five days using the town as a central base to visit local vineyards, olive groves, and surrounding hilltop villages.

faq.question: What is the best beach near Motovun?
faq.answer: The closest beaches are located in Novigrad and Poreč, approximately 25 to 30 kilometers away (a 30 to 40-minute drive). Karpinjan Beach in Novigrad features pebbles and pine shade, while Poreč offers numerous paved and rocky coves.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Motovun?
faq.answer: Having a car is highly recommended for a stay in Motovun. While the town itself is small and pedestrian-only, a vehicle is necessary to reach nearby wineries, regional hiking trails, and neighboring towns.

faq.question: Where to park in Motovun?
faq.answer: You must park at the designated municipal lots at the base of the hill or halfway up near the cemetery. From these lots, visitors either walk the steep cobblestone path or take a frequent municipal shuttle bus to the old town.

faq.question: Is Motovun good for families?
faq.answer: Motovun can be challenging for families with infants or toddlers due to steep gradients and cobblestone streets that are difficult for strollers. Older children typically enjoy walking the medieval defensive walls and exploring the surrounding nature trails.
